notes: scan049.N1. The page specifies pullback of an indexed chain by precomposition, presents X_{Delta_*} as a subobject of a product, and adds two remarks. Remark a replaces the ordered set by a category and the indexing assignment by a functor to closed subsets. Remark b contrasts the inclusion-induced relation on a bare indexing set with the weaker requirements on an already ordered indexing set. All literal abbreviations, signs, incomplete continuation marks and the apparent X-indexing slip are preserved.

scan049.N2. Targeted check of the displayed pullback rule: for alpha:Delta_{r prime}->Delta_r, alpha*(x,i_*)=(x,i_* composed with alpha). If beta:Delta_{r double-prime}->Delta_{r prime}, then beta* alpha*(x,i_*)=(x,(i_* composed with alpha) composed with beta)=(x,i_* composed with (alpha composed with beta))=(alpha composed with beta)*(x,i_*). The identity map acts identically. Thus the written rule has the expected contravariant composition law and leaves the X coordinate fixed. Restriction to the allowed chain-membership locus uses its preceding definition, which is not included in this packet.

scan049.N3. The literal left-hand letter in X mapsto X_i is a capital X, confirmed by crossed diagonals. An object/index variable such as i would be expected in an assignment to X_i, but the source page has X. This is recorded as an apparent authorial indexing slip, not corrected by the mathematical expectation.

scan049.N4. Targeted check of the relation in remark b: interpreting the written <= between subsets as inclusion, define i R j iff X_i is contained in X_j. Reflexivity and transitivity follow directly from inclusion. Antisymmetry need not hold for an arbitrary indexed family: choose two distinct labels 0 and 1 with X_0=X_1=F. Then 0 R 1 and 1 R 0 although 0 is not 1. The construction always gives a preorder; it gives a partial order if equal subsets force equal labels, or after quotienting by equality of associated subsets. The author’s relation d’ordre wording remains unchanged; whether that terminology includes preorders is a convention, not a transcription decision.

scan049.N5. The distinction in the last paragraph is valid. Noninjective monotone indexing is possible, for example a two-element chain with both labels assigned the same closed subset. Injective monotone indexing need not reflect order: take a two-element antichain and a nonempty space X, assign its labels the distinct closed subsets empty-set and X. The assignment is monotone because only identity inequalities occur, but the subset inclusion does not imply the corresponding index inequality. These examples separate injectivity and order reflection and support the author’s claim that neither is required by monotone indexing. The exact earlier statement numbered (1 prime b) is not in the packet and is not independently checked.

scan049.N6. The category-generalization remark and the full definition of X_{Delta_*} are carried as background. Formally, precomposition of composable chains is compatible with functorial images in the closed-subset category; this page alone does not supply every earlier topological or chain-membership convention needed for a full reconstruction. No outside theorem or source was used.

scan049.N7. Visual state: one actual cancellation crosses the trial formula in line 11. The a in ad is retraced but live. Four genuine insertions are marked: l’ens. ordonné before I; the raised category symbol before the comma; I un ens before sans; l’appl. croissante before I. Their leaders are not parentheses or strike lines. The apparent underline of plongement is the return of its g descender and is removed. Remarques has an independent underline, retained; H’s bold rendering of that same emphasized heading is treated as a representation difference only.

scan049.N8. Symbol and punctuation checks: both subset-order signs are literally <=, not subseteq. The first attached definition has vertical equality strokes with unaccented def on the right. The later def is unaccented above the equivalence. There are four trailing continuation marks after inclusions; the last is elongated. The inserted ens lacks a stop, while l’ens., l’appl., the later ens. and both occurrences of i.e. retain their visible stops. The live order-definition display ends with a separate point. The final reference has 1, a prime, b and two closing parentheses.

scan049.N9. Authorial page numeral 12 and pale foliation 48 are separate physical H omissions. The pale foliation is recorded as a margin element; the macro replacement does not change C’s digit reading. The two category symbols favor calligraphic C but preserve plain-C alternatives. The cancelled equality also remains explicitly uncertain. Both witnesses’ local illegibility flags are preserved in the comparison metadata wherever applicable.

scan049.N10. Blind adjudication retains the literal X indexing slip, vertical definition annotation, two script-C preferences and cancelled relation doubt. It now marks three small ambiguities: the dark point at the underline endpoint after Remarques, the fourth elongated continuation mark (point or dash), and the final e of inserted croissante. These qualify the certainty of N7-N8 without altering the preferred lexical readings. Ce soit and the wrapped au cas remain supported by their strokes.

checks.outcome: Identity and contravariant composition laws verified directly by associativity of function composition. Admissible-locus preservation remains conditional on the preceding definition.
Inclusion induces a reflexive transitive relation. A two-label repeated-subset example shows that antisymmetry requires an additional condition if relation d’ordre is intended to mean partial order.
Explicit two-element examples distinguish noninjective monotone indexing from injective indexing that fails to reflect order; no correction to the written assertion is needed.
